article: なぜ数学や計算機が好きなのか
scope: Compared the complete Japanese reflection and all twelve translations, including claims about fairness, rule clarity, mathematical validity, reproducibility, descriptions, categories, and references.
findings: Removed duplicate future dates, retained publication date 2022-09-23, and set lastmod to 2026-11-24 in every locale.
Framed the reasons as personal impressions and clarified that mathematical proof validity depends on assumptions, definitions, and inference rules.
Qualified same-input/same-output behavior: it applies to deterministic programs with the same program, input, state, and execution environment; randomness, time, and external data can change results.
Replaced the overly narrow math-cryptography-quantum category with existing mathematics and technology categories.
Added Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy and MIT OpenCourseWare references in all locales.

post/なぜ数学や計算機が好きなんだろう/index.en.md.source: post/なぜ数学や計算機が好きなんだろう/index.md
post/なぜ数学や計算機が好きなんだろう/index.en.md.summary: Compared the whole translation with Japanese, preserving the personal reflection while qualifying absolute statements about fairness, mathematical truth, and same-input/same-output behavior; added supporting references and corrected category metadata.

meaning.note: Compared the complete personal reflection in each locale. Preserved the author’s four reasons while clarifying that fairness and consistency are personal attractions, not universal properties.

terminology.note: Checked distinctions between mathematical proof, assumptions, definitions, inference rules, deterministic behavior, inputs, state, execution environment, randomness, time, and external data.

mathematics.note: Corrected the absolute claim that mathematical answers/theories are eternally true: proof validity is relative to assumptions, definitions, and inference rules. No formula or calculation occurs in the article.

code.note: Clarified that equal program outputs require deterministic behavior and matching program, input, state, and execution environment; nondeterministic/parallel behavior can yield variation.

links.note: Added and opened Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy on propositional logic/proofs and MIT OpenCourseWare material defining program determinism.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
The article presents personal reasons for liking mathematics and computers, not a technical survey of every formal system or programming model.
No mathematical formulas or executable code were included.
